answer: Shared inlet escrow prices coordination: each new identity deposits a fixed fee plus a per-reachable-agent charge into a common pool that pays existing agents for routing. An attacker pays that charge for every identity it creates, while honest agents reclaim their deposit after a clean voyage. The deposit is mirrored on a public ledger, so a fresh identity must pay again. Total cost remains fixed per identity, with counts S1 ~201, S2 ~120, S3 ~91, totaling ~412.
